title: Initiating: the initiation and kickoff workshops in a scenario
blurb: Match initiation work to the right activity and to the right topic of the project initiation or project kickoff workshop.
question: In Callowmere University's initiation stage, the teams agree general criteria every user story must meet before development starts, and later each team designs its own dashboard. Which workshops and topics are these?

teach.body: Initiating a project lays solid foundations so the business understands the work needed to deliver the project product before it commits significant money or resources. It defines scope, products, timeline, costs and the decision-making structure. In PRINCE2 Agile the project manager also defines the participants for two workshops, sets dates and invites people: the project initiation workshop, which shapes how the project will be run, and the project kickoff workshop, which shapes how the people will work together.

teach.body: The project Definition of Ready lists general, product-overarching criteria work must meet before development starts, such as clear requirements, resources, dependencies and measurable, prioritized acceptance criteria. The project Definition of Done lists general criteria for work to count as done and acceptable to users or the CPO, such as quality checks and guidelines. Both are set in the project initiation workshop; each team's own DoD sits in its product backlog.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Callowmere University's Student Support Hub
teach.body: Jamal Hussain runs the project initiation workshop. Everyone scores the Agilometer anonymously and the scores are combined. The group adds 'data handling approved by the data protection officer' to the project DoR and 'tested with assistive technology' to the project DoD. With the student design panel and the web team, they write a few fictional, needs-based personas. At the kickoff, the web team and Northmere's developers each design their own team dashboard, and the web team's skill matrix shows a gap in screen reader testing.

teach.text: Traps: criteria for starting work belong to the project DoR topic, not 'management approaches'. Team dashboards are co-created by each team at the kickoff; a PM who dictates one template defeats the workshop's purpose. The agile transformation plan, where needed, comes from the management approaches topic of the project initiation workshop, not from the agile enablement workshop.

items: Initiating: understand the work before committing significant spend.
Activities run from agreeing tailoring to 'request project authorization'; the release map is documented in 'prepare the project plan'.
Initiation workshop: Agilometer, approaches, project DoR and DoD, personas, release map, canvas refinement.
Kickoff workshop: intros, psychological safety, values, skill matrix, delegation matrix, dashboards.
Teams co-create their own dashboards; the project dashboard is created at the kickoff.

summary: You can now match initiation work to its activity, from agreeing tailoring to requesting project authorization. You can also place a discussion in the right topic of the project initiation or project kickoff workshop and spot when a kickoff choice undermines self-management.

A.q: Callowmere University's Student Support Hub project is in initiation. In the project initiation workshop, participants list general criteria that every user story must meet before development can start, such as clear requirements, known dependencies and measurable acceptance criteria. Under which topic should this happen?
A.why: The project Definition of Ready topic lists general, product-overarching criteria needed before development work starts (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: Management approaches are co-created for overall governance such as risk and quality; readiness criteria for stories have their own topic.
whyNot.1: The project DoD sets criteria for work to be done and acceptable to users, not criteria to start work.
whyNot.3: High-level release planning updates the release map with prioritized features and timelines.

A.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's click and collect project is in initiation. Project manager Patrick Dunne, with the project team, confirms the stage boundaries, the project tolerances and the procedures for escalation and decision-making. Which initiating activity is this?
A.why: Establishing project controls confirms and documents stage boundaries, project tolerances and escalation and decision-making procedures (Table 13.6).

whyNot.1: Agreeing the management approaches defines how change, communication, risk, quality and the rest will be managed.
whyNot.2: Preparing the project plan documents the release map, confirms people and resources and plans transition to operations.
whyNot.3: Agreeing tailoring requirements seeks lessons on tailoring and records the tailoring in the PID.

A.q: Draycott Precision Engineering's Smart Maintenance project is in initiation. At the project kickoff workshop, each member of the software team marks their current and planned skills in data engineering, sensor networks and testing, showing where the team has gaps and overlaps. Which topic is this?
A.why: The team skill matrix topic maps skills, gaps and overlaps; the matrix is completed collaboratively at the kickoff (Table 13.8, 7.4.1).

whyNot.0: The team delegation matrix clarifies who decides what, to simplify decisions and support self-management.
whyNot.1: Team values and norms agrees how the team will work together, building an agile culture.
whyNot.2: The psychological safety topic assesses how safe people feel to speak up and take risks.

B.q: Easterholm County Council's Care Online project is in initiation. Simon Archer reviews the management approaches for resources and costs, confirms which practitioners are available, sets out how the service will move into the social care operations team's daily use, and documents the release map. Which activity is this?
B.why: Preparing the project plan updates the project backlog if needed, identifies transition arrangements, confirms people and resources and documents the release map (Table 13.6).

whyNot.0: The full business case is a more detailed project canvas, not the release map and transition arrangements.
whyNot.2: Requesting project authorization shares the final canvas, PID and release map with the board once they are ready.
whyNot.3: Project controls cover stage boundaries, tolerances and escalation procedures.

B.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group's board has decided that Repairs Reimagined will be the first of several agile service changes, so it wants an agile transformation plan in place of the change management approach. The project is in initiation. Where should this be agreed?
options: Under 'Agilometer review' in the agile enablement workshop
Under 'management approaches' in the initiation workshop
Under 'team values and norms' in the kickoff workshop
Under 'project canvas refinement' in the initiation workshop
B.why: The management approaches topic of the project initiation workshop co-creates the approaches and, if needed, replaces the change management approach with the agile transformation plan (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: The enablement workshop reviews Agilometer results and adoption risks in directing; it does not produce the transformation plan.
whyNot.2: Team values and norms shapes one team's working culture, not the project's approach to organizational change.
whyNot.3: Canvas refinement aligns the project canvas with the updated release map; it does not replace a management approach.

B.q: Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project is in initiation. At the project kickoff workshop, the app team agrees which decisions it makes itself, which it makes after consulting its product owner, and which go to project manager Rhys Pengelly. Which topic is this?
B.why: The team delegation matrix makes decision authority transparent, simplifying decisions and empowering self-management (Table 13.8, 7.4.3).

whyNot.0: The skill matrix maps skills, gaps and overlaps, not who decides what.
whyNot.1: Values and norms set how the team works together and what it expects of each other, not decision levels.
whyNot.3: Team dashboards give transparency on progress; they do not define decision authority.

C.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's project is in initiation. Before the project kickoff workshop, Patrick Dunne designs one team dashboard template and tells both the e-commerce team and the store operations team to use it exactly as drawn. Is this an appropriate application of the 'initiating a project' process, and why?
options: Yes, because the project dashboard is created at the kickoff
Yes, because the PM pulls progress from team dashboards
No, because team dashboards are created at the first boundary
No, because each team should co-create its own dashboard
C.why: The kickoff workshop builds openness and self-management; team dashboards are co-created by each team, not dictated (13.4.4.2, Table 13.8).

whyNot.0: The project dashboard is created at the kickoff, but that does not justify dictating the teams' own dashboards.
whyNot.1: The PM does pull from team dashboards, but that is no reason for the PM to design them for the teams.
whyNot.2: The verdict is right but the reason is wrong: team dashboards are created at the kickoff, in initiation.

C.q: Callowmere University's project initiation workshop reaches the persona topic. The web team and student panel build personas from enrolment data on students' age, course and household income, and give each persona the name of a real student. Is this an appropriate application of the 'initiating a project' process, and why?
options: Yes, because persona definition is a topic of this workshop
Yes, because personas are written with the development team
No, because personas should be fictional and based on needs
No, because personas belong in the project canvas workshop
C.why: Personas are kept fictional and built on user needs rather than demographics such as age, occupation or income (6.4.1, Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: Persona definition is indeed a topic here, but that does not make demographic, real-person personas appropriate.
whyNot.1: Writing them with the development team is good practice, but these personas still break the needs-based, fictional rule.
whyNot.3: Persona definition is a topic of the project initiation workshop, so this is the right place for it.

C.q: Larkspur Rail's project initiation workshop reaches the Agilometer topic. Rhys Pengelly asks every participant, including team members and suppliers, to score the sliders anonymously, then combines the scores into one project Agilometer. Is this an appropriate application of the 'initiating a project' process, and why?
options: Yes, because all participants assess and the results are combined
Yes, because the board approves tolerances for agile decisions
No, because the agile coach should score it for the teams
No, because the Agilometer is first used in directing a project
C.why: In the Agilometer topic all participants assess the sliders, anonymously or in groups, and the results are gathered into one project Agilometer (Table 13.7).

whyNot.1: The executive does approve tolerances for agile decision-making, but that does not explain this Agilometer exercise.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 Agile has all participants assess the sliders; the coach does not score them on the teams' behalf.
whyNot.3: The first project Agilometer is built in the project initiation workshop; directing reassesses it later.

reteach.title: Moving into a shared house
reteach.question: Before a new group of housemates moves in, what do you agree about running the house, and what do you agree about living together?

blocks.h: The house rules and the housemates
blocks.body: First you agree how the house is run: the budget, who pays which bill, what counts as 'clean enough' before guests arrive and when the kitchen is ready for cooking. That is the project initiation workshop. Then the housemates meet: they share what they are good at, agree who decides what, and each person sets up their own shelf system. That is the kickoff.

blocks.text: A landlord who arrives with one shelf layout for everyone kills ownership. Teams co-create their own dashboards; the PM does not dictate them.

explain.body: Initiating establishes solid foundations so the business understands the work to deliver the project product before committing significant expenditure or resources. It defines scope, products, timeline, costs and the decision structure.

children.label: Initiating

test.q: Easterholm County Council's cabinet has agreed that Care Online is worth doing. Before it releases most of the grant, it wants a clear picture of the scope, products, timeline, costs and decision structure. Which process meets this need?
test.why: Initiating a project builds solid foundations so the business understands the work before committing significant expenditure (13.4.1).

whyNot.0: Starting up answers whether the project is viable and worthwhile, which the cabinet has already decided.
whyNot.1: A stage boundary reviews a completed stage and approves the next stage's plan.
whyNot.3: Directing is where the board makes decisions; the detailed picture it needs is built in initiating.

explain.body: When initiation is done, the PM shares the final project canvas, the PID and the release map with the board and formally requests authority to deliver the project. The board then decides in 'authorize the project'.

test.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group's initiation is complete. Sally Greaves sends the final project canvas, the PID and the release map to the project board and formally asks for authority to deliver Repairs Reimagined. Which activity is this?
test.why: In 'request project authorization' the PM shares the final canvas, PID and release map and formally requests authority to deliver (Table 13.6).

whyNot.0: Preparing the full business case produces a more detailed canvas; it does not ask the board for authority.
whyNot.1: Preparing the project plan documents the release map; the formal request comes afterwards.
whyNot.2: Establishing project controls sets boundaries, tolerances and escalation procedures.

explain.body: The project DoD topic lists general criteria for work on stories to count as done and acceptable to users or the CPO, such as quality checks and guidelines to follow. It sets a shared view of the quality needed before work is handed to users.

test.q: In Draycott Precision Engineering's project initiation workshop, the group agrees that every dashboard feature must pass a security check and be trialled by an engineer before it is handed to users. Under which topic should this be agreed?
test.why: The project DoD topic sets general criteria for work to be done and acceptable to users before hand-over (Table 13.7).

whyNot.0: The project DoR covers criteria for starting work, not for accepting finished work.
whyNot.2: Management approaches set overall governance; general completion criteria have their own topic.
whyNot.3: Persona definition describes key users to guide product decisions.

explain.body: The kickoff includes a psychological safety topic: an assessment of how safe people feel to speak up, take risks and challenge ideas. It supports the workshop's aim of an open, self-managing agile culture.

test.q: At Pinewick Home and Garden's project kickoff workshop, team members answer anonymous questions about whether they feel able to raise problems and challenge ideas, and discuss the results together. Which topic is this?
test.why: The psychological safety topic assesses how safe people feel to speak up and challenge ideas (Table 13.8, 2.7.4).

whyNot.1: Values and norms agree how the team will work together, rather than measuring how safe people feel.
whyNot.2: The delegation matrix sets who decides what.
whyNot.3: Icebreakers and intros build familiarity and connections, not an assessment of safety.
